requirement_title: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true
requirement_text:
# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234
Type: bug

## Requirement

The analyzer does not work if `SuppressSourceGeneration = true`. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

(The upstream issue contains no further text, repro or comments. Anything beyond this is derived.)

## Acceptance criteria

- With `SuppressSourceGeneration = true`, the MessagePack analyzer still reports its diagnostics (MsgPack0xx rules) for code that violates them. (derived)
- Behaviour with `SuppressSourceGeneration = true` matches version 3.1.0, where the analyzer worked. (derived)
- Behaviour with `SuppressSourceGeneration` unset or false does not change. (derived)
- Source generation itself stays suppressed when `SuppressSourceGeneration = true`. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

No comments on the issue.

findings.claim: No hunk touches how `SuppressSourceGeneration` is handled. The TypeCollector edits only add `continue` after the mixed-key diagnostic and de-duplicate keys before `Dictionary.Add`, and that applies to every type. Nothing in the diff makes the analyzer visit types marked `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]` again. So the core acceptance criterion (MsgPack0xx diagnostics are reported for such types) does not appear to be met.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests on head. If PublicPropertyWithoutKey_StillReportsMsgPack004 and PublicFieldWithoutKey_StillReportsMsgPack004 fail because the expected MsgPack004 is missing, the requirement is not met.

findings.claim: DepthStep changed from `reader.Depth >= MaximumObjectGraphDepth` to `>`. The reader can now go one level deeper than the configured MaximumObjectGraphDepth before InsufficientExecutionStackException is thrown. For example, with a limit of 3, Depth 3 no longer throws and nesting reaches 4. This weakens the documented stack-depth guard (the ledger records a hard limit of 500) for both trusted and untrusted data. It is also unrelated to REQ-2234, which concerns the analyzer and SuppressSourceGeneration.

receipt_plan.detail: Run DepthAndDuplicateKeyReceiptsTests.DepthStep_AtMaximumDepth_Throws. It sets reader.Depth = 3 with WithMaximumObjectGraphDepth(3) and expects DepthStep to throw. It passes on base and fails on head.

findings.claim: The change to MessagePackSecurity.DepthStep relaxes the depth check from >= to >, allowing one extra nesting level. No test in the diff covers it, and it has nothing to do with the requirement. An off-by-one on a security limit would survive the entire test suite.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack/MessagePackSecurity.cs:233 off-by-one: reader.Depth > this.MaximumObjectGraphDepth -> reader.Depth >= this.MaximumObjectGraphDepth; expected to survive because none of the added tests (analyzer tests or SuppressedSourceGenerationTests) exercise depth limits.

findings.claim: The ContainsKey guards in the second member-collection block (the field/property loop at lines ~1160-1180) have no dedicated test. The duplicate-key tests use properties, so they may exercise only one of the two loops. Removing the guard in the other loop would survive.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1163 remove-guard: if (!intMembers.ContainsKey(member.IntKey)) -> unconditional Add; expected to survive if the duplicate-key tests only exercise the other loop (e.g. properties vs. fields or a different type shape).

hunches.claim: `DepthStep` changed from `reader.Depth >= MaximumObjectGraphDepth` to `>`. This lets the reader go one level deeper than the configured maximum before it throws, which weakens the stack-depth protection (ledger L9: a depth limit of 500 even for trusted data). The requirement is an analyzer bug, so this runtime security change is out of scope and changes behaviour for every user.

receipt_plan.detail: Deserialize nested arrays of exactly MaximumObjectGraphDepth+1 levels (e.g. options.WithSecurity(MessagePackSecurity.TrustedData.WithMaximumObjectGraphDepth(2)) and bytes for [[[ ]]] read as object). Base throws InsufficientExecutionStackException (wrapped in MessagePackSerializationException); head succeeds. Also mutation: reverting `>` to `>=` should be killed by an existing depth test, which shows the change is behavioural.

hunches.claim: The new `ContainsKey` guards silently drop a second member that has a duplicate int or string key, and the new `continue` drops mixed-key members. Both apply when SuppressSourceGeneration is unset. Generator/analyzer behaviour for normal types therefore changes: previously `Dictionary.Add` threw, surfacing as AD0001/CS8785. The requirement says behaviour with SuppressSourceGeneration unset must not change, unless a MsgPack005 error is still reported for the duplicate.

receipt_plan.detail: VerifyCS test on a non-suppressed [MessagePackObject] with two members both [Key(0)]. Check whether MsgPack005 is reported on head; if no diagnostic appears and a formatter is generated that omits a member, behaviour changed silently.

hunches.claim: `intMembers.Add` became `if (!ContainsKey) Add`. When two members share the same [Key(n)], the second one is now silently dropped: there is no diagnostic and it is left out of the generated formatter. On base, the duplicate made the collector throw, so the problem was loud. On head, the second member's value is never serialized and always deserializes as default. That is silent data loss, and the analyzer (which shares TypeCollector) also stays silent.

receipt_plan.detail: Run DepthAndDuplicateKeyReceiptsTests.DuplicateIntKey_IsReportedOrBothMembersSerialized. It uses a type with two [Key(0)] properties and asserts that either a MsgPack error diagnostic is reported or the generated code references SecondValue. It fails on head.

hunches.claim: The same silent first-wins de-duplication applies to string keys: two members with the same [Key("x")] keep only the first, with no diagnostic. The int-key path at line 1163 and the string-key path at line 1179 in the second collector branch have the same behaviour.

receipt_plan.detail: Run a variant of DuplicateIntKey_IsReportedOrBothMembersSerialized that uses [Key("a")] on both properties. Expect no MsgPack error and no SecondValue in the generated output on head.

hunches.claim: DepthStep changed from `>=` to `>`, allowing one extra nesting level (depth MaximumObjectGraphDepth+1) before InsufficientExecutionStackException. Users' existing depth limit now accepts payloads that were previously rejected, which loosens a security limit and is unrelated to the SuppressSourceGeneration requirement. Edge-of-limit payloads change behavior without opt-in.

receipt_plan.detail: Set MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.WithMaximumObjectGraphDepth(N), deserialize a payload nested exactly N+1 levels (e.g., N+1 nested single-element arrays into object[]). Base throws InsufficientExecutionStackException; head succeeds. Also check existing depth-limit tests (e.g., MessagePackSecurityTests) for an off-by-one failure.

hunches.claim: In TypeCollector, a member whose key kind mismatches (mixing string and int keys) is now skipped via `continue` after reporting MsgPack005. Previously it fell through and was added to the members lists. The generated formatter for such types now omits that member, changing generated output. The type is already in error, so users who suppress the diagnostic could see changed output or lose members. This is not tied to the SuppressSourceGeneration requirement.

receipt_plan.detail: Run generator snapshot tests with a [MessagePackObject] type mixing [Key(0)] and [Key("a")] members. Diff generated formatter output between base and head, and confirm whether the members are dropped.

hunches.claim: Duplicate int/string keys are now silently deduplicated, with the first member kept, instead of throwing ArgumentException from Dictionary.Add. The generator/analyzer output for types with duplicate keys changes. The formatter is generated with only the first member, and the later one is dropped from output. If the duplicate-key diagnostic (MsgPack006) does not fire in all paths, a user's build previously failed and now silently produces a lossy formatter.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the generator on a type with two members sharing [Key(1)] (and a string-key variant), with and without SuppressSourceGeneration. Compare the diagnostics and generated formatter at base vs head to confirm MsgPack006 still fires and what is emitted.

hunches.claim: MessagePackSecurity.DepthStep changed from `reader.Depth >= MaximumObjectGraphDepth` to `>`, which allows one more nesting level than MaximumObjectGraphDepth. This loosens the depth/stack-overflow protection for untrusted data (and the 500 trusted-data stack limit in L9) by an off-by-one. It is unrelated to the analyzer / SuppressSourceGeneration requirement.

receipt_plan.detail: Set MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.WithMaximumObjectGraphDepth(N) and deserialize a payload nested exactly N levels (e.g. N nested single-element arrays). Base throws InsufficientExecutionStackException; head succeeds. Also run the existing MessagePackSecurityTests depth tests, which assert the boundary, to see them fail.

hunches.claim: In TypeCollector, a mixed int/string key member is now skipped via `continue` and duplicate keys are silently dropped via ContainsKey guards. Generation proceeds for malformed types instead of failing, so the formatter silently omits members. The generated deserializer then ignores data for those members. This also changes behavior beyond the stated requirement, and it matters when SuppressSourceGeneration is not set.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the generator snapshot tests with a type that has duplicate [Key(0)] members or mixed int/string keys. Compare the generated formatter at base and head to see whether members are omitted, and confirm MsgPack006/MsgPack005 diagnostics are still reported.

hunches.claim: The MessagePackSecurity.DepthStep comparison was changed from >= to >, which allows one more level of nesting than MaximumObjectGraphDepth. It is unrelated to REQ-2234 (analyzer with SuppressSourceGeneration) and loosens a security limit. Ledger L9 records the stack depth limit as a deliberate hardening.

receipt_plan.detail: Set MaximumObjectGraphDepth = N, deserialize a payload nested exactly N+1 deep. Base throws InsufficientExecutionStackException; head does not. Also cite [L9]: the depth limit is a recorded security hardening, and nothing in the requirement justifies relaxing it.

hunches.claim: The README and tests claim MsgPack011, MsgPack016 and MsgPack017 are not reported for suppressed types, but the visible hunks contain no change that implements this. Only duplicate-key skips were added in TypeCollector. The test SourceGenerationOnlyDiagnosticsAreNotReportedWhenSuppressed may pass or fail depending on code outside the shown scope.

receipt_plan.detail: Run SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.SourceGenerationOnlyDiagnosticsAreNotReportedWhenSuppressed on head and on base, and confirm the analyzer code path that gates MsgPack011/016/017 on SuppressSourceGeneration.

hunches.claim: The changes in the suppressed-generation analyzer path (the continue after DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys, and the ContainsKey guards) are covered only by whole-file analyzer tests. The mixed-key test expects a single MsgPack005 diagnostic and nothing else. Removing the `continue` would probably still pass, since the mismatched member would be added to the other dictionary without a crash. The test does not assert that the mismatched member is excluded from the member set.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1008 delete-statement: continue; -> (removed); expected to survive because MixedKeyKindsAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailure only asserts that diagnostics are reported, not how the mismatched member is treated.

hunches.claim: SuppressedSourceGenerationTests.NoFormatterIsGeneratedForSuppressedType and the round-trip test would pass on base as well, because suppression already worked at the generator level. They do not reproduce the reported bug, which is about analyzer diagnostics. Only the analyzer tests are relevant to the bug, and they may not distinguish base from head either. The head-only analyzer-path changes are the duplicate-key guards. MemberWithoutKeyIsReported, AllowPrivateRequiredIsReported and MemberTypeMustBeMessagePackObjectIsReported may already pass on base.

receipt_plan.detail: Run SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests and SuppressedSourceGenerationTests against the base build; tests that pass on base do not reproduce the bug.

hunches.claim: The README states that for suppressed types the analyzer reports MsgPack003/004/005/012/015 but not MsgPack011/016/017. No code in this diff implements or enforces that split, so the documentation describes behaviour this change does not deliver.

receipt_plan.detail: Compare README.md:1620-1632 with the TypeCollector hunks: none of them reference SuppressSourceGeneration or condition MsgPack011/016/017 on it.

hunches.claim: The source diff shows no change that makes the analyzer run for SuppressSourceGeneration types, such as removing an early return or skip condition. The tests for MsgPack004/015/003 therefore cover no changed line. Only the duplicate-key and mixed-key guards are changed, so the primary fix for the requirement may be missing or outside the supplied hunks.

receipt_plan.detail: Look for where SuppressSourceGeneration is checked in the analyzer/TypeCollector path; no hunk in this diff touches it.
